_doc: Planetary reference environments. Coordinates are planetocentric latitude / east-positive longitude (converted to -180..180 for GeoJSON). Body CRS: Moon IAU_2015:30100 (sphere R=1737.4 km, as used by the LOLA products); Mars IAU_2015:49900 (sphere R=3396.19 km, as used by the MOLA mosaic). status_class: verified_mission_site | candidate_region | representative_region. No entry is an approved permanent-base site. Literature values carry a verbatim quote and source; temperatures are surface/near-surface values whose physical meaning differs between bodies (see scientific_methodology.md).

gazetteer.note: The lunar south pole region is not a named IAU feature

references.name: Lunar south polar highlands (pole-centred region containing Artemis III candidate regions)
references.coord_source: definition: geographic south pole; Artemis III candidate regions listed by NASA 2024-10-28
references.status_note: NASA lists nine Artemis III candidate landing regions near the south pole (Peak near Cabeus B, Haworth, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton Plateau, Mons Mouton, Nobile Rim 1, Nobile Rim 2, de Gerlache Rim 2, Slater Plain); these are candidate regions, not selected sites and not approved permanent-base locations.

temperature_K.quote: These areas likely have temperatures of −50±10 °C, compared to the lunar equator where temperatures span from −150 °C to 100 °C.
temperature_K.note: Sunlit polar areas; converted -50 °C to 223 K.

illumination.value: Peaks along the rim of Shackleton are illuminated about 80–90% of each lunar orbit (literature); PSRs never illuminated
illumination.quote: Peaks along the rim of the crater are almost continually illuminated by sunlight, spending about 80–90% of each lunar orbit exposed to the Sun.

references.ice_evidence: Cold traps >80° latitude host most water-ice cold-trap area (Hayne et al. 2021 summarised in wiki:Lunar water).
hazards: steep crater walls and massif slopes
extreme thermal gradients between sunlit and shadowed terrain

references.name: Shackleton crater and rim vicinity
references.status_note: Frequently studied south-polar crater; 'Connecting Ridge' near Shackleton appeared on NASA's 2022 list of 13 regions but not on the 2024 refined list of nine (per The Register summary, 2024-10-29). Not an approved base site.

temperature_K.quote: For Shackleton, the average temperature was determined to be about 90 K (−183 °C; −298 °F), reaching 88 K at the crater floor.

illumination.value: rim peaks ~80–90% illuminated; interior in perpetual darkness
illumination.quote: Peaks along the rim of the crater are almost continually illuminated by sunlight, spending about 80–90% of each lunar orbit exposed to the Sun.

references.ice_evidence: LOLA reflectance analysis suggests up to 22% of Shackleton's surface may be covered in ice (wiki:Lunar water; Zuber et al. 2012).
hazards: ~4.2 km deep conical crater with steep walls

references.name: Malapert massif
references.coord_source: NASA Science image-detail 20100618 (85.99 S, 357.07 E); Allender et al. 2019 ASR doi:10.1016/j.asr.2018.08.032
references.status_note: 'Malapert Massif' is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate landing regions (NASA news release 2024-10-28).

temperature_K.quote: These areas likely have temperatures of −50±10 °C, compared to the lunar equator where temperatures span from −150 °C to 100 °C.
temperature_K.note: Regional value for illuminated south-polar terrain applied to Malapert; site-specific Diviner value not extracted (data gap).

illumination.value: two ridge regions illuminated ~74% of the lunar year (Bussey et al. 2010 as cited by Allender et al. 2019)
illumination.quote: The ridge of Malapert massif contains two regions which are illuminated for 74% of the lunar year (Bussey et al., 2010)

references.ice_evidence: Small-scale PSRs in surrounding area (Allender et al. 2019).
hazards: massif rises ~5 km; slopes 15–25° on ridge approaches (Allender et al. 2019)

references.name: Cabeus crater permanently shadowed region (LCROSS impact target)
references.coord_source: wiki:Cabeus (crater) GeoData (crater centre; LCROSS impact point lies within Cabeus)
references.status_note: Verified LCROSS impact target (2009-10-09); a mission impact site, not a landing or base site.

temperature_K.quote: This crater is sufficiently large that the temperature within the shaded region is below 100 K (−173 °C).

illumination.value: main crater lit ~25% of lunar day; western part in permanent shadow
illumination.quote: Because of the crater's location near the lunar south pole, the main part of the crater is illuminated by the Sun during only 25% of each lunar day.

references.ice_evidence: LCROSS ejecta water concentration 5.6 ± 2.9% by mass (Colaprete et al. 2010, as reported in wiki:Lunar water).

references.name: Marius Hills pit (mare volcanic dome field)
references.status_note: Candidate lava-tube skylight identified by SELENE and confirmed with LROC; representative subsurface-access environment, not a mission site.

temperature_K.quote: temperatures beyond the opening in permanent shadow would maintain a nearly constant temperature of ∼290 K
temperature_K.note: Horvath et al. 2022 modeled value for the Mare Tranquillitatis pit; applied to Marius pit as a lower-confidence proxy.

illumination.value: pit floor partly overhung (LROC Pits Atlas: Overhang=Y)

hazards: ~40 m deep pit (LROC atlas); boulder-covered floor; overhangs

references.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
references.status_note: Mare pit with possible cave extension (Horvath et al. 2022); representative subsurface environment.

temperature_K.quote: temperatures beyond the opening in permanent shadow would maintain a nearly constant temperature of ∼290 K

illumination.value: pit floor partly in permanent shadow beneath overhang
illumination.quote: wherever the Sun does not shine directly

references.name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base (mare regolith plains)
references.status_note: Verified 1969 crewed landing site (historic); not a base site.

temperature_K.quote: lunar equator where temperatures span from −150 °C to 100 °C
temperature_K.note: Only a range is sourced; no mean used.

illumination.value: equatorial day/night cycle (~29.5 Earth days synodic)

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).

references.name: Gale crater (Curiosity Bradbury Landing)

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).
temperature_K.note: Global mean; Gale expected near-surface air range −90 to 0 °C (wiki:Gale).

hazards: sharp rocks (wheel damage reported in mission literature, not quantified here)

references.name: Elysium Planitia volcanic plains (InSight landing site)

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).

references.ice_evidence: Possible ash-covered water ice reported near 5°N 150°E (Mars Express, wiki:Elysium Planitia) - debated.
hazards: low hazards; selected as smooth, flat plains

references.name: Vastitas Borealis periglacial plains (Phoenix landing site)

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).
temperature_K.note: Global mean; high-latitude site is colder (not quantified from fetched sources).

references.name: Planum Boreum north polar layered deposits
references.status_note: Representative polar ice environment; no landing site.

temperature_K.quote: Given a present mean annual surface temperature of 155 K and a geothermal gradient of 15°/km, the temperature at the base of the north polar cap likely falls between 200 and 215 K.
temperature_K.note: Clifford et al. 2000 (Icarus 144:210-242), section 2.4; mean annual surface temperature of the north polar cap. Excerpt: data/raw/literature/web/clifford2000_unl_excerpt.txt. Replaces the earlier null (only a minimum, 120 K, had been sourced from wiki:Climate of Mars).

references.ice_evidence: Ice cap mostly water ice (~95%) with dust layers (wiki:Planum Boreum).

references.name: Arsia Mons flank cave skylights (lava tubes / basaltic shield)
references.coord_source: wiki:Arsia Mons GeoData (239.91 E, volcano centre)
references.status_note: Seven putative cave entrances identified on Arsia flanks (Cushing et al. 2007 as summarised in wiki:Arsia Mons); some may be pits only.

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).
temperature_K.note: Global mean; high-altitude shield is colder (not quantified).

references.ice_evidence: Orographic water-ice cloud (atmospheric), not ground ice.
hazards: high elevation, thin atmosphere for EDL

references.name: Arcadia Planitia mid-latitude ground ice plains
references.status_note: Described as an area of interest for potential exploration because of near-surface excess ice; not a selected landing site.

temperature_K.quote: Differing in situ values have been reported for the average temperature on Mars, with a common value being −63 °C (210 K; −81 °F).

references.ice_evidence: Excess ice widespread in mid-latitudes, especially Arcadia Planitia (wiki).
mission_objectives: ISRU ground ice for human missions
